$comment: Canonical MCP tool catalog. tools/README.md is generated from this file by scripts/build-tools-doc.js. Platform snippets are the same command expressed in each client's config format.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.description: Drive a real browser through accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots.
tools.when_to_use: Use when an agent must click through a flow, fill a form, verify a UI change, or scrape a page that needs JavaScript. Prefer it over screenshot-based tools: the agent gets a structured tree it can reason about, not pixels.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.description: Inspect console, network, performance traces and DOM from a live Chrome session.
tools.when_to_use: Use for debugging a running app: console errors, failed requests, layout shifts, performance traces. Pair with Playwright MCP when you need both interaction and diagnostics.

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.description: Read repositories, issues, pull requests and actions through the GitHub API.
tools.when_to_use: Use when the task spans more than the local checkout: triaging issues, reviewing PRs, reading CI logs, or opening a PR. Needs a token with the minimum scopes for the repositories involved.

tools.name: Postgres MCP Pro
tools.description: Inspect schemas, run read-only queries, and get index and health advice.
tools.when_to_use: Use when the agent needs to understand a real database rather than guess at the schema: migrations, slow queries, index design, or data-shape checks. Point it at a read replica where possible.

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.description: Manage Supabase projects: SQL, migrations, logs, storage and edge functions.
tools.when_to_use: Use when the project is on Supabase and the task touches schema, auth, storage or edge functions. Scope the token to one project; do not hand it an organization-wide key.

tools.name: Context7
tools.description: Fetch version-specific documentation for libraries instead of relying on model memory.
tools.when_to_use: Use whenever an API may have changed since training: framework routers, SDK methods, config formats. It returns current docs and examples, which reduces hallucinated APIs.

tools.name: Exa MCP
tools.description: Semantic web search with full-page extraction.
tools.when_to_use: Use for research that needs primary sources: release notes, benchmarks, competitor docs. Better than a keyword search when the query is conceptual.

tools.name: Figma Context MCP
tools.description: Expose Figma file structure, components and styles to the agent.
tools.when_to_use: Use when implementing a design that exists in Figma. The agent gets node IDs, layout, tokens and text content instead of interpreting a screenshot.

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP
tools.description: Inspect and operate Workers, KV, R2, D1 and DNS.
tools.when_to_use: Use for deploy-adjacent work on Cloudflare: checking a Worker, reading logs, inspecting bindings. Keep the token scoped to the account and environment you are actually changing.

tools.name: Vercel MCP
tools.description: Read deployments, logs and project configuration from Vercel.
tools.when_to_use: Use after a deploy fails or when the agent needs to confirm what is actually running. Read-only is usually enough; avoid granting deploy rights to an autonomous loop.

tools.name: Filesystem MCP
tools.description: Scoped read/write access to a directory tree.
tools.when_to_use: Use when the agent must work across a directory the host tool does not already expose, or when you want an explicit allowlist. Pass the narrowest directory that solves the task.

tools.name: Sequential Thinking
tools.description: A scratchpad tool for multi-step reasoning with revision.
tools.when_to_use: Use for planning or diagnosis where the agent would otherwise rush. It is not a substitute for reading the code; it is a place to keep the plan visible and revisable.
